description: Staff rotation requires a clear record of who currently controls lockers, keys, overflow cages, and access codes so secure mail handling does not depend on informal verbal memory. All facilities are fictional.

user_profile.persona: 36-year-old operations coordinator responsible for secure storage access control
user_profile.context: Turnover and shift changes have made physical access knowledge too dependent on whoever happens to be present
user_profile.communication_style: Control-focused and concise, wants access responsibility tied to named assets and current holders

fact_sheet.fact: Javier Rossi is the Operations Coordinator at the Metroplex Distribution Center.
Lena Petrova is a Mailroom Clerk, employee ID 784-B, assigned to the day shift.
Marcus Thorne is the Night Shift Supervisor, employee ID 512-C.
The main mailroom is located in Wing B, Room B-112, at the Metroplex Distribution Center.
The secure overflow storage area is designated as Cage Bay 4, located in the sub-level warehouse.
Key KEY-MSTR-01 is the master key for all lockers in the LKR-A series (A01-A20).
Key KEY-CAGE-03 provides access to Overflow Cage C-03 in Cage Bay 4.
The key cabinet is a wall-mounted unit, model 'Securall SKC-50', located next to the supervisor's desk in Room B-112.
Key KEY-A14 is a single-use key for high-value package locker LKR-A14.
Locker LKR-A05 is designated for holding certified mail pending recipient verification.
The LKR-A series lockers are located along the north wall of Room B-112.
Locker LKR-A20 has a faulty latch and was reported for maintenance on November 14, 2023, under work order #MNT-9811.
Overflow Cage C-03 has dimensions of 10ft x 10ft x 8ft and is constructed of steel mesh.
Overflow Cage C-01 is currently at 75% capacity with unsorted bulk mail from the morning delivery.
Lena Petrova is the current holder of the master key KEY-MSTR-01, checked out at 07:55 on November 15, 2023.
Marcus Thorne is the assigned holder of Key KEY-CAGE-03 for the duration of the night shift (22:00-06:00).
Control of locker LKR-A05 was transferred from Marcus Thorne to Lena Petrova at 06:05 on November 15, 2023.
The access code for the main mailroom (Room B-112) is 8842#.
The mailroom access code 8842# is changed on the first Monday of every month by the Operations Coordinator.
The override code for the electronic key cabinet is 919-ALPHA-3, known only to Javier Rossi.
Shift handovers require a signed entry in the physical logbook, 'Logbook-MDC-B112', detailing the transfer of all keys and access cards.
Any lost key must be reported to the on-duty supervisor within 15 minutes of discovery.
Access to Cage Bay 4 requires dual authorization: one clerk and one supervisor must be present.
All key and asset assignments are digitally tracked in the 'KeyTrack Pro' system, accessible at https://apex.keytrackpro.local.
The 'KeyTrack Pro' system automatically sends an email notification to Javier Rossi when a master key is checked out for more than 8 hours.
The daily access log from the Room B-112 keypad is automatically archived to the shared drive at `//MDC-SERVER/logs/mailroom/`.
The physical asset handoff logbook, 'Logbook-MDC-B112', is kept on the metal lectern inside the entrance to Room B-112.
The primary contact for after-hours security issues is the Central Security Desk at extension 5555.
As of 14:30 on November 15, 2023, there are no unassigned secure assets; all keys and codes are accounted for.

user_needs.description: Who currently has the master key for the LKR-A series lockers?
Who is assigned the key for Overflow Cage C-03 during the night shift?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After asking about one major key, the user is likely to inquire about other critical keys.

user_needs.description: What issue was reported for locker LKR-A20, and under what work order was it logged?
What is the official procedure for recording shift handovers of keys?
Show me the last control transfer record for the certified mail locker, LKR-A05.
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After learning the general procedure for handovers, the user wants to see a specific, recent example.

user_needs.description: What digital system is used to track all key and asset assignments?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After asking about specific key assignments, the user will likely want to know about the official system used to track all such assignments.

user_needs.description: What is the access code for the main mailroom, Room B-112?
What is the policy for changing the mailroom access code?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After getting the current access code, the user is interested in the maintenance and security policy for that code.

user_needs.description: If a key is discovered to be lost, who must be notified and within what timeframe?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After learning about the system for tracking keys, a natural follow-up is to ask about the procedure for handling exceptions, such as a lost key.

user_needs.description: Who changes the mailroom access code, and how often is it changed?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After asking about the access-code policy, a direct follow-up is who performs the code change and on what schedule.

user_needs.description: What is the authorization protocol for entering Cage Bay 4?
Who should be contacted after hours about security issues involving secure-area access?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After inquiring about a high-security access protocol, a direct follow-up is who handles related secure-area access issues after hours.
